title: The microbiome and butyrate regulate energy metabolism and autophagy in the mammalian colon
authors: Donohoe DR, Garge N, Zhang X, Sun W, O'Connell TM, Bunger MK, et al.
population: Germ-free and conventionally raised male C57BL/6 mice aged 8 to 14 weeks
funder: National Institutes of Health (CA125237 to S.J.B.), American Institute of Cancer Research and The Prevent Cancer Foundation; germ-free mice were maintained by the National Gnotobiotic Resource Center (P40RRO118603 and P30 DK 34987).
result: In the colon of germ-free mice, NADH/NAD+ was 16-fold and ATP 56% lower than in conventionally raised mice, with no differences in liver, heart, kidney or testis. Germ-free colonocytes showed a 70% lower rate of oxidative phosphorylation, 31% less conversion of 13C-butyrate to CO2 and increased autophagy. Butyrate added ex vivo raised oxidative phosphorylation of germ-free colonocytes from 30% to 70% of conventional levels and suppressed autophagy; etomoxir, an inhibitor of fatty-acid oxidation, prevented both effects. Colonisation with complete microbiota or with Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens restored oxidative phosphorylation and ATP.
